note: Clean pass with two disclosed caveats. SOURCE: PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0261914 (Gomez, Brown, Watson & Stavropoulos 2022), CC BY 4.0; the study's own S2 File .sav (s002) is the level-1 source. MAPPING: the IRW item codes ARE that .sav's column names (data/gomez_2022_qcae.py melts QCAE_COLS unchanged, no positional or renaming step), and 27 of the 31 columns carry a numbered variable label holding the item verbatim (e.g. QCAE15 = '15. I can easily tell if someone else wants to enter a conversation.'), so those 27 are data_labels with no inference. The FOUR reverse-scored columns QCAE1r, QCAE2r, QCAE17r and QCAE29r carry NO variable label and no value labels -- they are the authors' reverse-recoded versions of QCAE items 1, 2, 17 and 29 (the same four the sibling deposit queiros_2018_qcae ships as QCAE_1_R/2_R/17_R/29_R), so their wording was taken from the canonical QCAE (Reniers et al. 2011, J Pers Assess 93(1):84-95) keyed by item number, transcribed from the EMERGE/UCSD reproduction (emerge.ucsd.edu/r_3punmrvubfwa4xc/), which prints all 31 items and marks the four reverse-scored ones. mapping_basis is therefore recorded as paper_explicit rather than data_labels -- the conservative of the two -- and Step 5b was done rather than claimed exempt. WHICH REVERSE ITEM IS WHICH: EMERGE lists items in subscale-grouped order, not Reniers' original numbering, so the four wordings had to be keyed back to numbers 1/2/17/29. Queiros et al. (2018, PLOS ONE 13(6):e0197755, CC BY) name item 17 by number and print it -- 'item 17 from the peripheral responsivity subscale ("It is hard for me to see why some things upset people so much")' -- and add that 'the three remaining items that compose this subscale (items 2, 11 and 29) address emotional responses to social contexts that are detached to the subject, such as narrative works of art (movies, plays, novels)'. That fixes 17, and the data agree: QCAE17r has by far the weakest PER item-rest correlation (+0.219 vs +0.568/+0.521/+0.609) and correlates only +0.145..+0.221 with the three narrative items, matching the loading of .29 this paper itself reports for item 17. QCAE1r correlates +0.542 with the Online Simulation rest but only +0.172 with PER, so it is the single reverse-worded OS item ('I sometimes find it difficult to see things from the "other guy's" point of view.'). NOT ESTABLISHED BY DATA: QCAE2r vs QCAE29r, the two remaining narrative PER items -- item-rest +0.568 vs +0.609, mutual r +0.573, and no published quantity is keyed to their text. Their assignment rests on Reniers' documented item sourcing (items 1-6 from the IRI, whose reverse Fantasy item is 'I am usually objective when I watch a film or play...'; items 15-29 from the Empathy Quotient, which supplies 'I usually stay emotionally detached when watching a film.'). Hence status PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. ANCHORS, and a paper/data contradiction: the .sav value labels give 1 = Strongly Disagree, 2 = Slightly Disagree, 3 = Slightly Agree, 4 = Strongly Agree for all 27 labelled items, and data/gomez_2022_qcae.py's LIKERT_MAP uses the same coding; the paper's Methods states the reverse ('1 (strongly agree), 2 (slightly agree), 3 (slightly disagree), and 4 (strongly disagree)'). The labels win on the numbers: summing as stored gives Cognitive Empathy M = 58.80 (SD 9.57) and Affective M = 34.57 (5.82), against published norms of 57.14 (8.28) / 33.75 (5.51) in Powell (2018, n = 844) and 59.42 (9.12) / 36.76 (6.08) in Reniers et al. (2011); the flipped reading would give 36.20 and 25.43. The paper's sentence is an error. FLIPPED ANCHORS ON FOUR ITEMS: because QCAE1r/2r/17r/29r are stored ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED (all four correlate POSITIVELY with their own subscale rest; a raw reverse-worded item would correlate negatively), their shipped option_text is flipped -- resp 1 = 'Strongly Agree' ... resp 4 = 'Strongly Disagree' -- so that each resp value names what the respondent actually selected. Same move as burkert_2019_whoqol_bref. TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS: the .sav labels' leading item numbering ('15. ') and the non-breaking space after it were stripped; nothing else was altered, so the source's own missing terminal full stops (QCAE6, QCAE18) are kept as-is. instructions and section_prompt are blank: neither the .sav nor the paper publishes participant-facing instructions, and nothing was invented. correct_response blank (attitude scale). STEP 3b: the table name, dictionary Description and live content all agree -- 31 items, 1-4, and the .sav labels are QCAE items; the other instruments in the same file (TOSCA, SIAS-6, SPS-6, BIS/BAS, ERQ, ATQ) are present only as totals and are not in this table. RIGHTS: no restriction found that fires either 2026-09-04 trigger. The QCAE is not fee-licensed and no no-redistribution clause from Reniers et al. could be found; the deposit that supplied 27 of the 31 items is CC BY 4.0 and Queiros et al. (CC BY) publishes item 17 in full. The only restrictive sentence located is Taylor & Francis's standard per-article PDF boilerplate ('This article may be used for research, teaching and private study purposes...'), which is the publisher's term for the ARTICLE FILE, not the rights holder's term for the instrument, and IRW copied no wording from that PDF. Under the ECR-R/source-licence rule that is not a block; silence is permission.
public_note: Two things to know before using this table. (1) The four reverse-worded items -- QCAE1r, QCAE2r, QCAE17r and QCAE29r -- are stored already reverse-scored, so for those four (and only those four) resp 1 means the respondent chose 'Strongly Agree' and resp 4 'Strongly Disagree'; the response-option text shipped here is flipped accordingly, and no further reversal is needed to score the scale. (2) The source paper's Methods describes the scale as running 1 (strongly agree) to 4 (strongly disagree), which contradicts the deposited .sav's own value labels; the labels are correct -- summing as stored reproduces the published QCAE norms (Cognitive M = 58.8 vs 57.1 in Powell 2018; Affective M = 34.6 vs 33.8), while the paper's direction would give 36.2 and 25.4. Wording for the four unlabelled reverse items comes from the canonical QCAE rather than this study's file; items 2 and 29, both narrative-context items, cannot be told apart from the data and were assigned from the instrument's documented item sourcing.
